controls_available: Difficulty 3 uses a 9x8 isometric course with five pictured strokes: ROLL 2, ROLL 1, CHIP 1, CHIP 2, and ROLL 2; the generated hand is shuffled and each card is spent once.
The visible course exposes fairway, sand, water, ramp, cup, elevation, and ramp-direction information; the level-3 profile has 3 water decoys, 2 ramps, 12 other decoys, and chip clearance 2.

The simplified outcome-affecting UI is mouse-based: click a pictured stroke card, then click one of four labelled north/east/south/west compass buttons. The environment declares a keyboard channel, but this mechanic installs no keyboard control.

A normal screenshot-only solution reads the visible course and hand, plans the legal card order and directions, then performs the five card/direction interactions; CERTIFY SUNKEN BALL is final administrative submission.

grouped_control_modes.name: simplified_stroke
grouped_control_modes.scope: All card-selection and compass-direction stroke dispatches across the five strokes and all generated instances

clause_i.reason: For the grouped simplified stroke mode across generated instances, an action-only q cannot generally select the correct mouse target: the generator applies a seed-dependent board/direction reflection and shuffles the card positions, while the correct card and direction are determined from the visible course and hand. This is a static visual/planning dependency, not a temporal one.

clause_ii.reason: A single current screenshot is sufficient for the visual choice: it contains the isometric tiles, surfaces, elevations, ramp arrows, cup, current ball, and visible hand. Thus a bounded-window policy can choose the next card and compass direction without observing motion; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.

clause_iii.reason: After any input boundary, the course and hand remain unchanged until another input. The browser's transition calculation and ball/card mutation run synchronously inside the direction-click dispatch; the canvas cloud and water marks are drawn statically, and CSS hover/selection/drag transitions are presentation only. Certification is administrative. The 180-second play allowance is only a deadline and cannot provide the required non-clock task-state degradation, so no Delta > 0 and no bounded window can satisfy clause (iii).

common_visible_process: None. There is no visible autonomous task-state process shared by an outcome-affecting control mode: the board, cup, hand, and ball change only on a synchronous stroke dispatch, while the runner deadline does not change the mechanic state.

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already yields No because clause (iii) has no autonomous non-clock task evolution; the pre-run override is therefore not applicable and no percentage is asserted.

source_evidence.claim: The exact level-3 profile is medium, uses a 9x8 board, has a five-stroke action plan, one route sand landing, 3 water hazards, 2 ramps, 12 decoys, and chip clearance 2.
The exact simplified interface is card click followed by one of four labelled compass buttons; the configured play allowance is 180 seconds, observation window 0 ms, and one frame.
Generation selects the supplied difficulty profile, applies its condition parameters, then uses a seed only to construct a static transform, palette, and course data.
The action plan creates fixed route tiles, cards, and a fixed transformed solution; there is no time or autonomous update in generation.
Decoy surfaces and transformed tile coordinates are generated once, and the course stores fixed start, cup, and movement rules.
The transition routine reads the current state and card/direction and returns a synchronous legal landing or error; it contains no clock or autonomous update.
Simplified clicks arm a card and compass clicks call dispatch; successful dispatch immediately appends an event, mutates ball and used-card state, redraws, and updates the counter.
Only certification performs the asynchronous result submission, while render constructs the UI and performs the initial hand/compass/scene draw; certification is not a moving task phase.
The only transition effects are card hover/selection/drag styling and button/readout styling; they do not alter course state or grading.
The independent movement replay applies fixed surface, water, height, ramp, chip, and sand rules to submitted strokes, with no elapsed-time input.
Grading replays only numbered stroke and certification events, checks the exact settled state and exact hand, and has no timer or task-state evolution.
The task verifier loads the exported result and Cloudstep grader and returns the replay grade; it introduces no timing mechanic.
The solver's simplified input path is card click then direction click; its private ground-truth solution and 120 ms test waits are implementation evidence, not task-time behavior.
